summary: **Dated: 16[th ] March, 2026 Present: Hon`ble Ms. Seema Gupta, Officiating Chairperson Hon`ble Mr. Virender Bhat, Judicial Member** 1. The present Appeal No. 58 of 2020 has been filed by M/s Shree Cement Limited **(hereinafter referred to as “Appellant”)** under Section 111 of the Electricity Act, 2003 challenging the order dated 26.11.2019 (“ **Impugned Order** ”) passed by the Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission in O.P. No.22 of 2019 whereby the State Commission had dismissed the Petition filed by the Appellant herein while upholding the deduction of liquidated damages by the Respondent No.2. 9. On 24.11.2017, the Appellant executed a Power Purchase Agreement with Respondent Nos. 3 to 7 for sale of energy in terms of the agreed conditions. 10. The Appellant is aggrieved that notwithstanding the occurrence of a Force Majeure event and the Appellant’s offer to supply power from an alternate source, Respondent No. 2 raised a claim for compensation under Article 6.2 of the PPA amounting to Rs. 60,50,077/-, which was subsequently revised to Rs. 29,72,647/- 11. The State Commission, passed the impugned order dated 26.11.2019, dismissing the Petition filed by the Appellant and held that though offer of supply from alternate sources between 24.11.2017 – 30.11.2017 can be considered as valid offer but for the days 22.11.2017 & 23.11.2017 cannot be construed as valid offer and Appellant is liable to pay Liquidated damages. In addition, The Appellant is also held liable for the payment of open access charges of about Rs 12,81,0101 to the extent power is not availed by the respondents. Aggrieved thereby, the Appellant has preferred the present Appeal on 09.01.2020. supply power from an alternative source under article 5.1.4 of the PPA, wherein it is expressly provided that if the Seller is unable to supply power up to the Contracted Capacity from the Delivery Point, except due to a Force Majeure event, it shall supply power from an alternative generation source with the consent of the Procurer(s); by invoking Article 5.1.4, the Appellant has itself acknowledged that the situation does not fall within the scope of the Force Majeure clause and therefore the Appellant’s plea of _Force Majeure_ is untenable, unsubstantiated, and evidently raised only to evade liability towards Liquidated Damages under the terms of the Agreement. _The Affected Party shall give intimation to the other Party of any event of Force, Majeure immediately but not later than 24 Hours._ _To the extent not prevented by a Force Majeure event, the Affected Party shall continue to perform its obligations pursuant to this Agreement. The Affected Party shall use its reasonable efforts to mitigate the effect of any event of Force Majeure as soon as practicable._ 21. With regard to the contention that Respondents, in their reply, has admitted for non-levy of LD for the period from 22.11.2017 to 30.11.2017, we take note that Respondents, in their reply to the petition filed by the Appellant, at para (k) & (m) has submitted that Liquidated damages are payable only for the period 19.11.2017 to 21.11.2017, and that no LD is being levied from 22.11.2017 onwards, as the Appellant has offered supply from alternate source. In para (n) & (o) it has contested the contention of Appellant with regard to supply of contracted energy from 22.11.2017 to 30.11.2017. The respondents have excluded the entire period from 22.11.2017 to 30.11.2017, from the availability calculation, whereas Appellant in its calculation has considered deemed availability of generation for the entire period from 22.11.2017 to 30.11.2017, which is not in line with submissions of Respondents in the Reply. In these circumstances, the reliance placed by the Appellant on the statements made in the Reply of the Respondents is misplaced and of no assistance to the case of the Appellant. 25. From the operative portion of the Impugned Order, it is evident that there is no specific or categorical direction issued to the Appellant to pay the Open Access charges so calculated. The denial of relief to the Appellant was premised only on the reasoning that the aggregate liability, when liquidated damages and open access charges are considered together, exceeded the deductions already effected by the Respondents. It is further noted that the Respondents had not raised any claim towards Open Access charges for the relevant period either prior to the passing of the Impugned Order or subsequent thereto. Neither Respondents nor the Appellant has drawn our attention towards pending claim for levy of open access charges for the period under consideration. Thus, it is evident that no independent demand or assertion of liability on account of Open Access charges was ever made by the Respondents against the Appellant. The Appellant has, in fact, confined its prayer to seeking withdrawal of the finding in the Impugned order relating to the levy of Open Access charges. 26. In view of the foregoing, and particularly in the absence of any operative direction fastening liability upon the Appellant, coupled with the Respondents’ own conduct in not raising any claim for Open Access charges during the period under consideration, we hold that the levy of Open Access charges cannot be sustained. The Appellant cannot be burdened with a liability which has neither been claimed by the Respondents nor specifically directed in the operative part of the Order. Accordingly, the prayer of the Appellant seeking withdrawal of the direction of levy of Open Access charges merits acceptance. 27. In view of the above deliberation, the calculation of liquidated damages as determined in the Impugned Order is hereby upheld. However, the Impugned Order stands modified to the extent of the liability worked out upon the Appellant towards Open Access Charges, which is set aside. 29. The appeal is partly allowed in the above terms. All pending IAs, if any, stands disposed of in above terms of this order.
title: M/S SHREE CEMENT LIMITED VERSUS KARNATAKA ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION Ors
